explanation: A dictionary locates each cache node, and a linked list tracks recency. Lookup and reinsertion move a node to the front; reinsertion deliberately preserves its old price. New entries evict the back node when capacity is reached.
timeComplexity: O(1) expected per Lookup, Insert and Erase; O(c) to Initialize an existing cache Hash lookup and linked-order changes take expected constant time per operation.
spaceComplexity: O(c), where c is capacity At most capacity keys, prices and order nodes are retained.
attribution: Original EPI Practice C++ implementation and reset-aware operation wrapper, independently authored from the public problem contract and repository-authored C# algorithm. Uses the unchanged local EPI Judge serialization and test framework APIs; upstream reference sources are not modified.
correctness: The dictionary and linked list contain exactly the same keys, and list order is most-recent to least-recent. Lookup and reinsertion move the located node to the front without changing its stored price. Removing the back node before a new insertion therefore evicts exactly the least-recent key; erasure removes both representations together.
walkthrough: With capacity 2, insert (1,10), insert (2,20), reinsert (1,99), then insert (3,30). Key 1 still costs 10 and is recent, so key 2 is evicted. Lookups return 10, −1 and 30 for keys 1, 2 and 3. JSON arguments contain one command array. LruCache initializes capacity; lookup/erase commands include expected results (erase uses 1/0). The wrapper observes all commands succeeding as true; the class itself has separate lookup, insert and erase results.
edgeCases: Reinserting a key preserves its old price.
A missing lookup returns −1 and does not add a key.
Initialize resets all stored entries and recency.
